'''Egil Sigurd Lillestøl''' (19 March 1938 — 27 September 2021) was a Norwegian experimental [[Elementary particle physics|elementary particle physicist]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Egil Lillestøl (1938–2021)|url=https://home.cern/news/obituary/cern/egil-lillestol-1938-2021|access-date=2021-10-14|language=en}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
Lillestøl graduated in 1964 from the [[University of Bergen]] and obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the same university in 1970.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Lillestøl|first=Egil|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=75wXAQAAMAAJ|title=Study of annihilation of antiprotons at rest in hydrogen to multipion final states|publisher=University of Bergen|year=1970|location=Bergen|language=en}}</ref> He was appointed associate professor at the university the same year and appointed professor in 1984. Leading up to his professorship in Bergen, he had been a fellow at [[CERN]] (1964–1967) in [[Geneva]], Switzerland and a guest researcher at [[Collège de France]] (1973) in [[Paris]].

== Career ==
Lillestøl was involved in experiments carried out at [[DESY]], [[Hamburg]], Germany, where he was central in the [[PLUTO detector|PLUTO Collaboration]], and at  CERN, where he was member of the [[DELPHI experiment|DELPHI Collaboration]]. Furthermore, he was instrumental in the process to develop a long-term funding model allowing Norwegian research groups to participate in the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] experiments [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] and [[ALICE experiment|ALICE]].

Still affiliated with University of Bergen, Lillestøl took up positions at CERN. He was Deputy Head of CERN's Physics Division from 1990 to 1992. After this he split his time between the university and CERN. From 1992 to 2009 he was Head of the European School of Particle Physics, CERN Schools of Physics.

=== Physics communication ===
Lillestøl put a strong emphasis on physics communication. In addition to teaching at university level and giving presentations at international conferences, he also communicated complex physics concepts to both school children and the general public. He was a regular lecturer at the [[European Space Camp]] from 2001 onwards.

=== Energy and climate ===
Lillestøl  was also interested in global energy issues and an opportunity to solve the world's energy problems using [[thorium-based nuclear power]]. He advocated establishing the use of nuclear power to solve the international energy crisis, and that Norway should build a prototype of a [[Thorium fuel cycle|thorium reactor]].<ref>Ursin, Lars Holger (9. november 2006): [http://forskning.no/alternativ-energi-energi-fysikk-kjernefysikk-radioaktivitet/2008/02/trygg-kjernekraft-kan-snu «Trygg kjernekraft kan snu energikrisen»], ''UiB, Forskning.no''</ref> He was founding member of the [[International Thorium Energy Committee]].<ref name=":0" />

Lillestøl was critical of the Norwegian climate debate and pointed out that the Earth's climate is very complicated, and climate science is young and still has a long way to go before one can hope to find complete explanations for the Earth's climate variations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forskning.no/a/1182577|title=Kronikk: Jordens klima og liv på geologisk tidsskala|last=Professor|first=Egil Lillestøl|work=forskning.no|language=no|date=30 May 2009|access-date=16 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nrk.no/vestland/--hysterisk-klimadebatt-1.4849901|title=- Hysterisk klimadebatt|last=Skien|first=John Gunnar|work=NRK|language=nb-NO|date=18 February 2008|access-date=16 June 2021}}</ref>

== Bibliography ==
Lillestøl co-authored the popular science book ''The Search for Infinity'' (1994),<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Fraser|first1=Gordon|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vk6SQgAACAAJ|title=The Search for Infinity: Solving the Mysteries of the Universe|last2=Lillestøl|first2=Egil|last3=Sellevåg|first3=Inge|date=1994|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|isbn=978-1-85732-280-4|language=en}}</ref> which has been translated into eight other languages. He also contributed to the preparation of the Norwegian textbook ''Generell fysikk for universiteter og høgskoler'' (General Physics for Universities and University Colleges) (2001).<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Lillestøl|first1=Egil|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xUsctwAACAAJ|title=Generell fysikk for universiteter og høgskoler: Varmelære og elektromagnetisme. Bind 2|last2=Lien|first2=Jan R.|last3=Hunderi|first3=Ola|date=2001|publisher=Universitetsforlaget|isbn=978-82-15-00006-0|language=no}}</ref> Furthermore, he was also one of the main drivers behind the [[UNESCO]]-supported traveling exhibition “Science bringing nations together”,<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1037575/|title=Science bringing nations together|date=2001|publisher=CERN|editor-last=CERN. Geneva|location=Geneva|editor-last2=Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Dubna}}</ref> organised jointly by [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research|JINR]] and [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1999|title=Collaboration in science and technology|journal=Annual Report: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research|volume=1999|pages=30}}</ref>

His scientific output, as recorded by the database [[INSPIRE-HEP|Inspire-HEP]], amount closely to hundred works.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 August 2023 |title=Inspire-HEP author profile: Egil Lillestøl |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature?q=a%20E.Lillestol.1 |access-date=30 August 2023 |website=Inspire-HEP}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2007, he was awarded the [[Research Council of Norway's Award for Excellence in Communication of Science]] for "dissemination of basic physics to schoolchildren and the public".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2011-06-07|title=Prisvinnarar – Norges forskningsråd|url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/no/Prisvinnarar/1138785824319|access-date=2021-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607123812/http://www.forskningsradet.no/no/Prisvinnarar/1138785824319|archive-date=2011-06-07}}</ref>

Egil Lillestøl was a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ntva.no/medlemmer/egil-lillestol/|title=Egil Lillestøl {{!}}{{!}} NTVA|date=14 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714231631/http://www.ntva.no/medlemmer/egil-lillestol/|access-date=4 October 2021|archive-date=2020-07-14}}</ref> and the [[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-29|title=Gruppe II Fysikk – DKNVS|url=https://www.dknvs.no/akademiet/medlemmer/gruppe-ii-fysikk/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029200007/https://www.dknvs.no/akademiet/medlemmer/gruppe-ii-fysikk/|access-date=2021-10-04|archive-date=2020-10-29}}</ref>
